payload.rationale:
To resolve to Yes, the 2026 annual average must exceed 1.28 C (since it must be above both 1.28 C and the 2025 value of 1.19 C). The sum of the first 8 months is 9.79 C, averaging ~1.22 C. To reach an annual average above 1.28 C, the sum for the entire year must exceed 15.36 C, meaning the remaining 4 months (September-December) must sum to >5.57 C, or average >1.3925 C. 

The strongest reason this estimate could be too low is that a very strong El Niño is currently developing and strengthening, which typically boosts global temperatures significantly in the latter part of the year. August already hit 1.40 C, showing that such high anomalies are attainable. 

The strongest reason this estimate could be too high is that an average of >1.39 C over four consecutive months is an exceptionally high hurdle. Only one month in 2026 (August) has reached this level so far, and maintaining it consistently through the end of the year leaves very little room for natural variability or temporary dips in the anomaly.
limitations: The annual target remains unknown, with four months missing.
No ENSO forecast or fitted annual-temperature predictive distribution is supplied.
